report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations has changed since the AI Act's original adoption. As enacted in 2024, these obligations were due to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence), but a subsequent amending regulation—the "AI Omnibus"—pushed this date back to 2 December 2027 (high confidence). High-risk systems embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) face a later date of 2 August 2028 (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As originally adopted in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after the Regulation's entry into force (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Date
Following the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI), the application date for Annex III obligations was moved to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). The amended Article 113 text specifies that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III classification and obligations), except Article 6(5), apply from this new date (medium confidence) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

This change followed a clear legislative process: the Commission adopted the Digital Omnibus on AI proposal on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)); the Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)); and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

Commentary attributes the delay to concerns that harmonised technical standards needed for compliance were not ready in time, risking the original 2 August 2026 deadline (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Notably, the Commission's original Omnibus proposal had suggested a flexible timeline—adjustable by up to 16 months and contingent on confirmation that standards and tools were available—rather than a fixed date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Annex I Products: A Later Deadline
High-risk AI systems that are safety components of, or are themselves, products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) are subject to a later application date of 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Grandfathering Provisions
Operators of high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the relevant Chapter III application date remain subject to the Regulation only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Several lower-authority and undated sources (e.g., [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)) continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the applicable deadline, apparently not reflecting the Omnibus amendment (low confidence). This likely reflects outdated publication timing rather than a genuine legal dispute.

It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date is now fully fixed, or whether some conditionality on standards-readiness from the original Commission proposal survived into the final text—sources describing the final outcome present it as a firm date, but this is not explicitly confirmed (medium confidence claims only). One source identifies the amending instrument as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," but this is low confidence and not corroborated by official EU sources ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). Similarly, a claim describing 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as mere "backstop" dates is low confidence and uncorroborated ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- The precise official title and number of the amending regulation is inconsistently referenced across sources; it is unclear whether all references point to a single legal instrument.
- Whether any conditionality on standards availability survived in the final adopted text, versus a hard 2 December 2027 deadline, is not definitively confirmed.
- How the "significant design change" grandfathering rule interacts with the shift from the original 2 August 2026 date to the revised 2 December 2027 date is not addressed by available sources.

## Methodology Note
This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations has changed since the AI Act's original adoption. As enacted in 2024, these obligations were due to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence), but a subsequent amending regulation—the "AI Omnibus"—pushed this date back to 2 December 2027 (high confidence). High-risk systems embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) face a later date of 2 August 2028 (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As originally adopted in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after the Regulation's entry into force (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Date
Following the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI), the application date for Annex III obligations was moved to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). The amended Article 113 text specifies that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III classification and obligations), except Article 6(5), apply from this new date (medium confidence) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

This change followed a clear legislative process: the Commission adopted the Digital Omnibus on AI proposal on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)); the Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)); and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

Commentary attributes the delay to concerns that harmonised technical standards needed for compliance were not ready in time, risking the original 2 August 2026 deadline (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Notably, the Commission's original Omnibus proposal had suggested a flexible timeline—adjustable by up to 16 months and contingent on confirmation that standards and tools were available—rather than a fixed date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Annex I Products: A Later Deadline
High-risk AI systems that are safety components of, or are themselves, products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) are subject to a later application date of 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Grandfathering Provisions
Operators of high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the relevant Chapter III application date remain subject to the Regulation only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Several lower-authority and undated sources (e.g., [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)) continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the applicable deadline, apparently not reflecting the Omnibus amendment (low confidence). This likely reflects outdated publication timing rather than a genuine legal dispute.

It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date is now fully fixed, or whether some conditionality on standards-readiness from the original Commission proposal survived into the final text—sources describing the final outcome present it as a firm date, but this is not explicitly confirmed (medium confidence claims only). One source identifies the amending instrument as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," but this is low confidence and not corroborated by official EU sources ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). Similarly, a claim describing 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as mere "backstop" dates is low confidence and uncorroborated ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- The precise official title and number of the amending regulation is inconsistently referenced across sources; it is unclear whether all references point to a single legal instrument.
- Whether any conditionality on standards availability survived in the final adopted text, versus a hard 2 December 2027 deadline, is not definitively confirmed.
- How the "significant design change" grandfathering rule interacts with the shift from the original 2 August 2026 date to the revised 2 December 2027 date is not addressed by available sources.
